data.notes_barbara:
Overlapping customers; Different business model; Different delivery model

Both serve small and midsize employers, but BBSI uses a PEO/co-employment model rather than HCM software. Scored 1 under the rubric’s customer-overlap rule.
data.notes_matthew: BBSI is a PEO (professional employer organization), which is 94% of its revenue. It handles payroll, human resources and benefits for small businesses through co-employment, meaning it becomes the legal employer of record. So the customer is similar to Paylocity's but the product is a service, not software.

data.reason: Professional employer organization model with workers' compensation insurance and staffing, a different business from payroll software.
PEO with workers' compensation insurance and staffing; co-employment service model, not a software subscription.
Outsourced payroll, HR and benefits administration with per-employee fees to small and mid-sized businesses.

Both sell payroll and HR support to US small and mid-sized employers, so customers overlap. The offerings differ. Paylocity sells a hosted HCM software platform. BBSI sells PEO outsourcing bundled with workers' compensation insurance, staffing and local consultants. That gives them different revenue models and risk profiles. The overlap is real but partial, so this is adjacent, not direct.

BBSI provides payroll and HR administration plus a unified HRIS that automates those processes for businesses across sizes and industries. Its PEO and consulting delivery differs, but the explicit software and customer overlap satisfies both criteria.
